answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique PGP key with web-of-trust signatures. With a key signed by ten people, a single quill check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since a key signed by ten people takes calendar time as well as money — and the kernel is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the ember of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
